Not reported because obscure or unconfirmed: Lullaby (In Hammersbach) from Op. 27, violin & piano ed. W. Henley (Joseph Williams, London 1902); 'Petite reine - Berceuse' (1886, pub. 1907 per Wikipedia; no IMSLP page found). WebSearch budget ran out during this composer, so the gap check is partial.

verdicts.note: Checked although verify=false: Allegretto on GEDGE, C major, composed 1888 (not 1885), first published by Schott, London 1889 (plate 3696), dedicated to the Misses Gedge, Malvern.

Checked: Etudes caractéristiques, Op. 24, solo violin, five studies (A-E), F.W. Chanot, London 1892 (plate 711), dedicated to Adolf Pollitzer. Duration not documented - the queued 12 min is unverified.

No published violin & piano edition found. IMSLP's Gavotte (1885, dedicated to Dr C.W. Buck) lists only an orchestral arrangement (A. Schmid, Schott), a string-orchestra arrangement (J. Morrison, 1989) and a Schott piano version (ca.1886, plate 24133); the page sits in the Manuscripts category and the key is not stated.
Checked: Offertoire (Andante religioso), F major, violin & piano, composed 1893, first published by Boosey & Co., 1903 (IMSLP; Wikipedia dates it 1903).
Checked: IMSLP '3 Pieces for Violin and Piano, Op.4' (Idylle / Pastourelle / Virelai); Pastourelle published by Novello ca.1914 (plate 13757).
Checked: IMSLP '3 Pieces for Violin and Piano, Op.4'; Virelai published by Novello ca.1914 (plate 13759).

Manuscript-only: Reminiscences (1877, D major, inscribed to Oswin Grainger) survives in BL Add. MS 57912; Wikipedia marks it 'manuscript'; the only score on IMSLP is an amateur typeset by John Morrison (2019).
Manuscript-only one-page exercise ('Exercise for the 3rd finger', written 1877, copied for Heifetz in 1920); only an amateur typeset (J. Morrison, 2019) on IMSLP; not a repertoire piece.
Very easy first-position teaching exercises (Op. 22, 1892) - below the catalogue's grade 3-4 entry level and method-book material, although the work exists (IMSLP/Wikipedia).

verdicts.title: Canto popolare (In Moonlight), from In the South, Op. 50 (arr.)
verdicts.note: A violin & piano edition exists (Novello, London 1904; editor Isabella Jaeger; a viola version ed. Hobday has the same imprint), but IMSLP names no arranger and I found nothing showing it is 'Elgar's own version'; Wikipedia's list files the Canto popolare under viola & piano. Added '(arr.)' in line with other unnamed arrangements.
